title: LP2-15 square-derived title keys
question: Do five specified number sequences from the LP2-15 square turn its nine-rune heading into two complete words under fixed GP29 arithmetic?
reader_question: Does the LP2-15 square decode its short heading?
summary: Exact Stage I title replay checks 30 complete two-word outputs from five square-derived key sequences, both directions and three arithmetic signs; none passes the source vocabulary gate.
finding: The pinned source reports 0/30 complete two-word vocabulary passes. Its 20,000 seeded random nine-rune subtraction keys also yield zero passes. Independent site-text arithmetic reproduces every candidate output; optional full source replay reproduces the vocabulary verdicts and control byte-for-byte.
limitations: A strict vocabulary miss for these 30 fixed candidates cannot exclude other square routes, shifts, spelling conventions, keys, vocabularies or a different cipher on the LP2-15 body. Zero hits in 20,000 random keys does not mean a zero chance probability.
next_steps: A new square-title proposal should fix its traversal, key conversion, arithmetic and full two-word prediction before checking the heading, then make an additional prediction beyond those nine runes.

scope.representation: First nine archived LP2-15 runes with the visible 4+5 word boundary, and its printed 16-value number square. GP29 zero-based indices.
scope.procedure: Run only the pinned Stage I title function; independently derive all five 16-value sequences, compare the constructed cell-value set with the printed panel and recalculate all 30 two-word outputs from Liberpedia page text.
scope.parameters: Five declared sequences x outward/inward x ciphertext-key, ciphertext+key and key-ciphertext, modulo 29; first nine key values; complete two-word vocabulary gate; 20,000 seeded random-key controls.
scope.exclusions: Alternate source routes, key starts, body text, vocabulary, GP spelling, punctuation choices and additional cipher layers.

review.kind: exact public-source Stage I title-function replay with independent site-text arithmetic
review.reviewer: Thirty decoded pairs independently reproduced; pinned source title output including 20,000-key control reproduced byte-for-byte

reproduction.environment: Bundled checks use Python 3 standard library. Optional vocabulary/control replay needs NumPy and the external pinned source checkout.

visuals.caption: Five source number sequences, two directions and three arithmetic rules produce 30 complete heading candidates; none passes the source's two-word vocabulary gate.
